scope: Curated summaries of OpenJDK processes. Follow the linked governing documents and the target project's current rules; these summaries do not grant approval or perform administrative actions.

processes.title: Project Lead responsibilities
processes.summary: Coordinate technical direction, maintain project infrastructure and publish a quarterly activity report. The lead appoints Authors and designates repositories requiring formal review.
steps: Keep contact details, mailing lists, web content and repositories current.
Publish recent activity each quarter; getProjectActivity summarizes integrated changes, authors and first-time contributors for the period, and getPullRequestTriage shows what is waiting.
Delegate obligations to Committers as appropriate; full authority can only be delegated temporarily.

processes.title: Appoint an Author
processes.summary: A contributor requests Author status from the Project Lead with references to at least two sponsored contributions. Author status still requires a sponsor for integration.
steps: Collect the contribution references and assess continued involvement; getContributorRecord lists the contributor's integrated pull requests.
The lead notifies the registrar; registration and the census update follow.

processes.title: Elect a Committer
processes.summary: A project Committer nominates a contributor. Current project Committers vote by Lazy Consensus: no unresolved vetoes. Prior Author status is not mandatory.
steps: Check the nominee's record with getContributorRecord and the project's own significance criteria.
Publish qualifications and a two-week deadline on the project list; searchMailingList finds CFV and Result threads.
Announce the result there and notify the registrar on approval.

processes.title: Elect a Reviewer
processes.summary: A project Reviewer nominates a project Committer. Current Reviewers use Three-Vote Consensus: no vetoes and three Yes votes, or unanimity with fewer eligible voters.
steps: Check the nominee's record with getContributorRecord and the project's own criteria.
Publish qualifications and a two-week deadline on the project list; searchMailingList finds CFV and Result threads.
Announce the result and notify the registrar on approval.

processes.title: Run and close a vote
processes.summary: Identify the electorate and voting rule before opening a vote. Votes are public; only each voter's latest vote counts. Vetoes require justification.
steps: Use the process-specific notice and deadline, normally two weeks; searchMailingList locates the CFV thread and replies, but vote tallies must be read from the messages.
Resolve vetoes and announce the tally and outcome; early consensus completion requires every eligible voter to vote Yes.

processes.title: Change the Project Lead
processes.summary: Sponsoring Group Leads nominate and select a successor using Three-Vote Consensus. If they cannot agree, the OpenJDK Lead selects a nominee.
steps: Coordinate succession with the sponsoring Group Leads.
Consult the bylaws for exceptional removal and appeal procedures.

processes.title: Review, sponsor and integrate a change
processes.summary: Use the target branch's contribution rules, issue tracker and tests. Check the latest PR revision, Skara progress and required reviews before requesting integration.
steps: Use getContributionContext and getBuildGuidance for the selected repository and ref.
Use getOpenJdkReview to inspect checks, reviews with Skara roles, blockers and issue links; getPullRequestTriage groups a repository's open pull requests.
The author requests /integrate; a contributor without commit rights needs an eligible Committer to /sponsor. Skara pushes the commit and closes the pull request with the integrated label.

processes.title: Compatibility and Specification Review
processes.appliesTo: JDK exported interfaces and significant compatibility changes
processes.summary: Assess CSR needs early for interface, specification or broad behavioral changes. A source review or JEP does not replace CSR approval.
steps: Draft the CSR with the compatibility impact and proposed specification; obtain review from an engineer familiar with the area. searchIssues with type CSR lists pending requests.
For the one-phase process, the assignee finalizes the request for CSR review and approval.
For early feedback use Proposed, then CSR Provisional review, followed by Finalized and Approved; Provisional is not final approval.

processes.title: Propose and deliver a JEP
processes.appliesTo: JDK features and significant infrastructure or process changes
processes.summary: Build agreement on a JEP, record the proposal in JBS and distinguish roadmap candidacy from targeting a release. JEP 1 links to the revised JEP 2.0 workflow.
steps: Draft, review and endorse the proposal, then submit it for candidacy.
Document an engineering plan before proposing a target release; getReleaseSchedule shows the release's rampdown dates, and the Project Lead decides targeting after evaluating the plan and consensus.
Track implementation, tests and documentation through Integrated and Complete; the Project Lead marks delivery when the release ships.

processes.title: Backport a fix
processes.summary: Track the original commit and the exact target repository and branch. Review and approval requirements vary by updates project and release phase.
steps: Check existing backport evidence with getIssueFixStatus (JBS fix versions) and getBackportStatus (commit provenance).
Create a Skara backport PR from the original commit; explain adaptations and test the target branch.
Follow target-specific review and maintainer approval rules before integration; a clean application alone does not establish approval.
